chunks: 2121 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Glorious:
"...wherein the resident and the visitor are equal..."

He said: "It was not proper for doors to be made on the houses of Makkah, because the pilgrims had the right to stay with them in their houses, in the courtyard of the house, until they completed their rites. Indeed, the first one who made doors for the houses of Makkah was Mu'awiyah."

key_terms.الْعَاكِفُ: the resident or one settled there

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about the meaning of “the resident and the visitor are equal” in Makkah?
ai.summary: This narration explains the verse as indicating equal access in Makkah between resident inhabitants and visiting pilgrims. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام presents it as a basis for the pilgrims' right to lodge in the open areas of Makkan homes until they complete the rites of hajj, and notes historically that Mu'awiyah was the first to install doors on those houses.
